members.tone: Condemns without naming the fault, covering plain offensiveness and shading into outright ill will, where *hateful* puts the malice at the centre.
Absolute rather than pointed - the condemnation is total in degree where *nasty* keeps a needling edge.
Contempt by way of defilement - it treats what it hits as unclean rather than merely offensive, a heavier verdict than *grotty*.
The disgust in *dirty* pushed to its limit, vileness so thorough it lands as a moral verdict.
Contempt thrown off casually - the despising is real but carries none of the weight that *filthy* brings to it.
British and slangy, it registers offensiveness as squalid distaste rather than the moral condemnation in *filthy*.
Makes ill will the whole of the charge, naming the malice itself where *nasty* only shades toward it.
The plainest word for malice, stating the ill will flatly where *hateful* makes it sound monstrous.

families.axis: bare nearness or resemblance → settled, felt intimacy

members.tone: The plain measure of nearness in relevance or relationship, stating the proximity without the warmth or the suspicion the rest of the set add.
Measuring and cool - it rates a resemblance as very close while stopping short of calling it the same thing.
Blunter than *approximate* for the same degree of resemblance - it asserts the likeness flatly instead of hedging it.
Warm and a little grand - closeness with good cheer inside it, heartier than the merely matey *chummy*.
Informal and light - friendly association on easy terms, without the depth *intimate* claims.
The doubled informal form makes the closeness emphatic and knowing where *chummy* keeps it mild.
Blunt informal shorthand for being closely associated, reporting the tie without the warmth *chummy* supplies.

members.gloss: held together as by social or cultural ties
members.tone: Approving of cohesion - the bond is what holds people together, structural where *dear* is personal.

members.gloss: held together as by social or cultural ties
members.tone: The open form spells the binding out and reads more deliberate and descriptive than the compact *close-knit*.
Closeness figured as trust - what passes inside it is entrusted, where *chummy* is merely companionable.
Insinuating - the closeness is treated as connivance, so the snugness of the word becomes the accusation.
The British spelling carrying the same imputation of connivance, warmth named in order to be distrusted.

members.gloss: with or in a close or intimate relationship
members.tone: Affectionate and avowed - the close relationship is felt as fondness, where *thick* merely reports the association.

members.gloss: with or in a close or intimate relationship
members.tone: Plain and understated for the same close relationship - it vouches for the bond rather than professing feeling as *dear* does.

members.gloss: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
members.tone: Closeness worn as ease - an established friendship that needs no ceremony, less ardent than *intimate*.

members.gloss: having mutual interests or affections; of established friendship
members.tone: The strongest claim in the set - mutual affection and settled friendship, closer and more private than *familiar*.

families.axis: a bare statement that something is not there → total emptiness, or existence ended altogether

members.gloss: not having existence or being or actuality
members.tone: Flat and absolute - the thing simply has no being, without the sense in *missing* that it was expected somewhere.
Registers the nonexistence as a deficiency rather than a bare fact, which *absent* does not.
Neutral and faintly formal, stating the nonexistence with none of the note of shortfall in *lacking*.
Points at the gap - the nonexistence is felt as a hole where something belonged.
The most judging of these - the nonexistence reads as falling short of a mark, not merely as nothing being there.
Bleak - the total lack is a desolate condition rather than the cool fact *devoid* states.
Severe - the complete lack sounds like deprivation, emptiness that hurts.
Formal and absolute, naming total emptiness while passing no verdict on it.
The approving member - the same complete lack is a relief, the absent thing one you are better off without.
Light and wry - complete absence made to sound blameless, the opposite colouring to *destitute*.

members.gloss: no longer existing or inaccessible through loss or destruction
members.tone: Technical and dry - marks the thing as gone through loss or destruction and judges nothing about it.
Carries the drama of a disappearance - existence not merely denied but ended, where *nonexistent* implies no before.

families.axis: easy to see → so complete it needs no proof or explanation

members.tone: The flat baseline of the group: a thing takes no effort to see or grasp, without *palpable*'s pressure or *axiomatic*'s claim about proof.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: The lightest way here of saying the thing shows itself — it reports the showing rather than pressing it, unlike *unmistakable*.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: Plain and unemphatic: the thing is simply there to be seen, with none of the display *manifest* makes of it.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: Formal and expansive — the thing does not merely show but puts itself on show, a grander word than *evident* for the same clarity.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: Pushes the showing towards touch, so the thing is felt as much as seen — heavier in the hand than *apparent*.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: Formal and declarative: the clarity is stated as settled fact rather than offered as an impression, where *palpable* appeals to the senses.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: The homeliest word here — clarity with no ceremony at all, exactly what *manifest* supplies in excess.

members.gloss: clearly revealed to the mind or the senses or judgment
members.tone: Works by ruling out the alternative: the thing cannot be read as anything else, a firmer guarantee than *apparent* gives.
Formal and absolute — the thing stands with no argument put behind it, a larger claim than being merely *evident*.
The plainer word for the same standing as *axiomatic*: the thing carries its own warrant and asks for none to be brought.
An ordinary-language phrase that concedes the standing rather than asserting it — the thing passes without argument instead of being shown to need none.

members.gloss: capable of being demonstrated or proved
members.tone: Shifts from what is seen to what can be shown: the clarity is available on demand rather than immediate, unlike *obvious*.

members.gloss: capable of being demonstrated or proved
members.tone: The blunter twin of *demonstrable*, resting the whole claim on proof being possible.
Technical and unemphatic — it flags the thing as clearly there and does nothing more with it, where *manifest* makes a display.

members.gloss: so obvious as to be easily solved or decided
members.tone: Informal and conclusive: the obviousness is enough to settle the matter, not merely to be seen — a force *plain* never reaches.
The thing supplies its own account, so nothing need be added to it — a different job from *obvious*, which only says it is easy to grasp.
Plain, unraised approval - it states the pleasure and satisfaction given and leaves it there, where *delightful* insists.
Approval with esteem in it - it asks you to look up at the thing rather than merely enjoy it, a graver register than *charming*.
Warm and disarming - the pleasure sounds like an appeal exerted on you, gentler than *delightful*'s enthusiasm.
Enthusiastic - the pleasure is raised to a high pitch and given an edge of entertainment that *pleasing* lacks.
Savouring - it makes high pleasure sound like something relished, richer and more indulgent than *delightful*.
Understated to the edge of neutrality - it concedes that pleasure is afforded without any warmth of praise behind it.
Extravagant - praise pitched at the ceiling and past plausibility, far louder than *pleasing*.
Slangy and clipped - the same top-of-the-scale praise as *fabulous*, tossed off rather than declared.
All-purpose and colourless - it grants no more than the capacity to please, where *pleasing* reports pleasure actually given.

members.gloss: pleasing to the mind or feeling
members.tone: Sober and faintly formal - it puts the pleasure in the mind or the feelings rather than on the surface, weightier than *sweet*.

members.gloss: pleasing to the mind or feeling
members.tone: Warm and informal - the same inward pleasure as *gratifying*, but tender and unguarded rather than composed.
It measures pleasing by the favour won rather than by the pleasure given, which tilts it away from praising the thing at all, unlike *charming*.

families.axis: difficulty framed as a stretch worth making → difficulty framed as a predicament no one would want

members.gloss: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
members.tone: Flat and unemotive - it registers that effort is required to do, grasp or bear the thing, without hinting whether that effort is worth spending, as *challenging* does.

members.gloss: not easy; requiring great physical or mental effort to accomplish or comprehend or endure
members.tone: The blunt, plain-spoken version of *difficult* for the same demand, taking effort of body, mind or endurance as it comes and softening none of it.

members.gloss: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
members.tone: Approving - it treats the full call on your abilities and resources as a reach worth making rather than a weight to be borne.

members.gloss: requiring full use of your abilities or resources
members.tone: Turns that same full call on everything you have into an invitation to rise to it, so the demand reads as a spur where *problematic* reads as a fault.

members.gloss: difficult to accomplish; demanding considerable mental effort and skill
members.tone: Formal and weighty - it dwells on the sustained mental effort and skill the thing exacts before it will be accomplished, heavier in the mouth than *hard*.

members.gloss: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
members.tone: Mildly disapproving - the difficulty sits in the handling, since any move you make risks the pain or embarrassment the thing carries.

members.gloss: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
members.tone: Puts the discomfort squarely on the face of whoever has to deal with it, naming the exposure that *awkward* leaves implied.

members.gloss: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
members.tone: Informal - it makes the trouble something you are caught in and cannot step cleanly out of, lighter in tone than *unenviable* and no easier to escape.

members.gloss: hard to deal with; especially causing pain or embarrassment
members.tone: An understated verdict that condemns by observation - the thing is framed as unwished-for, and the word damns it without raising its voice.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: Puts the great mental demand where understanding fails - the thing does not merely resist solution, it leaves you at a loss.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: The difficulty is in the slipping away: comprehension seems within reach and will not close on it, unlike the frank obstruction of *knotty*.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: Gives the mental demand a shape - a tangle to be picked apart strand by strand, rather than the blank wall of *baffling*.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: Labels the demanding thing a problem outright, a mild verdict against it where *tough* only reports the demand.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: Stiffer and more formal than *problematic* for the same verdict, its extra syllable adding weight rather than force.

members.gloss: making great mental demands; hard to comprehend or solve or believe
members.tone: Informal and almost respectful of the difficulty - it sizes up the mental demand as something to be taken on and says nothing against it.
Warns of a snare - the difficulty is concealed until you are into it, so the word marks the thing as harder than it lets on.

families.axis: requiring more than usual → severe and impossible to satisfy

members.gloss: requiring more than usually expected or thought due; especially great patience and effort and skill
members.tone: Plain and unheated - it names the size of what is asked without ruling on whether asking it is fair, where *hard-to-please* has already convicted someone.
The formal, cool-surfaced twin of *exacting* - the same insistence on precision, pitched at a distance.
Puts the weight on the standard itself, so the precision reads as a measure to be met rather than a temper to be humoured.
Disparaging - the fussiness makes the demand a flaw in the person, which *exacting* never does.
The open spelling carries the same verdict but reads as a running remark about someone rather than a label fixed to them.

members.gloss: demanding or needing attention, affection, or reassurance to an excessive degree
members.tone: Belittling and intimate - the excess is emotional appetite, and the word tips toward pity where *hard-to-please* stays at irritation.

members.gloss: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
members.tone: Approving - the strictness registers as discipline worth having, where *tight* only pinches.

members.gloss: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
members.tone: Cool and administrative, stating how tightly the rules bind without either praising or resenting the binding.

members.gloss: demanding strict attention to rules and procedures
members.tone: The informal one, and the constriction is felt - the rules squeeze rather than uphold anything.

members.gloss: severe and unremitting in making demands
members.tone: Adds a forbidding manner to the severity - the unrelenting demand arrives with a chill that *strict* does not carry.

members.gloss: severe and unremitting in making demands
members.tone: The flat word for the same unrelenting severity, stating it without colouring it as harshness.

families.axis: a light leaning that could go either way → a tendency fixed hard enough to be counted on

members.gloss: (often followed by ‘to’) having a preference, disposition, or tendency
members.tone: Mild and non-committal - the leaning is stated lightly enough to leave room for doing otherwise, where *prone* fixes it in place.
Neutral but predictive - it treats the leaning as a matter of the subject's nature, so what follows sounds expected rather than merely possible.
Formal and dry - the leaning sounds like a settled arrangement of temperament rather than an appetite, cooler than *given*.
Blunt and settled - the disposition sounds ingrained rather than merely present, heavier and more everyday than *disposed*.
Puts the disposition in the subject's cast of mind rather than in what it does, which is what separates it from *tending*.
The plainest of these - it names the direction of the leaning and claims nothing about temperament or liking.

members.gloss: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
members.tone: Warm - the leaning is felt as liking rather than as mere direction, which is what lifts it clear of *inclined*.

members.gloss: (followed by ‘of’ or ‘to’) having a strong preference or liking for
members.tone: Lighter and more indulgent than *fond* - it casts the strong liking as a weakness cheerfully admitted.

members.gloss: having a tendency (to); often used in combination
members.tone: Flat and fixing - it states the tendency as a standing liability rather than a leaning, and welds straight onto whatever is tended toward.

members.gloss: having more than the average number of accidents
members.tone: Mildly damning - it turns a count of mishaps into a standing property of whatever it is aimed at, so the accidents read as owed to it rather than to chance.
